thesis: 截至09:06 SGT，市场的绑定约束已从“主要央行是否同步加息”切换为“油价与长端收益率的同步回落，能否在BOJ决议前真正解除全球融资压力”：美股周四出现明显风险修复，S&P 500涨1.14%、Nasdaq涨1.69%，美国10年期收益率回落至约4.93%；周五亚洲早盘Brent进一步降至103.74美元，但USDJPY升至156.15、日本8月核心CPI仅1.7%却仍面对市场普遍预期的BOJ加息至1.25%。因此今天真正的裁决不是风险资产已经反弹，而是BOJ能否在低于2%的核心CPI与弱日元/高进口成本之间完成加息，同时不重新点燃日元融资与全球期限溢价冲击。
dominant_narrative: 过去24小时的跨资产链条出现了“政策仍偏紧、金融条件却战术性缓和”的重要分化。Fed加息后的第二个交易日，美股由科技与半导体带动反弹，10年美债收益率回到约4.93%，BoE虽以6比3维持3.75%利率并警告通胀可能在2027年初超过4%，却同时暂停主动售债并永久停止出售2049年以后到期的长债，英国30年期国债收益率因此大幅回落，说明央行可以通过资产负债表节奏缓冲政策利率的紧缩冲击。能源端也在同方向缓和：Brent周五亚洲早盘降至103.74美元，Saudi预计数日内恢复East-West pipeline约一半能力；但Reuters最新调查显示实际受损泵站从两座增至三座，完整修复仍可能需要5至6周，所以价格回落是物流缓冲而非地缘风险消失。日本成为今天唯一剩余的一级政策闸门：8月全国核心CPI仅1.7%、低于1.8%预期，但USDJPY已升至156.15，油价与进口成本仍高，市场此前普遍预计BOJ加息25bp至1.25%。与此同时，中国继续把资源向先进制造和国产AI算力倾斜，Huawei称国内AI设备需求超过供给；CoreWeave再融资30亿美元可转债、GlobalFoundries与Marvell扩充AI数据中心连接芯片产能，说明AI资本开支仍强，但越来越依赖债务资本与制造扩张。若BOJ加息后日元走强而JGB/全球长端保持稳定，本周的“央行收紧→风险资产崩塌”链条会进一步失效；若BOJ给出更快正常化信号并带动日元融资成本与全球长端重新上行，则周四的风险修复更可能只是事件后的短暂喘息。

what_changed.yesterday: Sep17 Morning treated the BoE decision as an unresolved test of synchronized tightening.
what_changed.today: The BoE held Bank Rate at 3.75% by 6-3, warned inflation could exceed 4%, but simultaneously paused active gilt sales and permanently stopped selling 2049+ gilts.
what_changed.why_it_matters: The decision shows policy rates can stay restrictive while balance-sheet policy relieves term premium; UK long yields fell sharply rather than reinforcing the global duration shock.

what_changed.yesterday: Sep17 Morning showed U.S. risk assets still under pressure after the Fed hike and the 10Y near 5%.
what_changed.today: S&P 500 rose 1.14%, Nasdaq 1.69%, Russell 0.55% and the U.S. 10Y fell to about 4.93%.
what_changed.why_it_matters: The first full post-Fed session rejected a simple 'hike equals broader deleveraging' narrative, shifting the burden of proof to whether lower yields and oil can persist.

what_changed.today: Reuters reported three East-West pumping stations were damaged and full repairs may take 5–6 weeks, while markets also expect about half the capacity to return within days.
what_changed.why_it_matters: The physical risk is more severe than the price action suggests; tactical supply relief can coexist with a persistent geopolitical risk premium.

what_changed.why_it_matters: Below-target core inflation gives the BOJ a softer inflation signal, but weak yen and imported-cost risks still support normalization; guidance now matters at least as much as the first 25bp move.

top_catalysts.event: BOJ decision today tests whether a widely expected hike to 1.25% strengthens the yen without reigniting global duration stress
top_catalysts.event_time_et: 2026-09-18 — release time 尚无法可靠确认
top_catalysts.event_time_sgt: 2026-09-18 — release time 尚无法可靠确认
top_catalysts.what_happened: Japan's August national core CPI rose 1.7% y/y, below the 1.8% Reuters consensus, while USDJPY traded around 156.15 and the Nikkei rose 0.8% in early Friday trade. A Reuters poll before the meeting showed economists expecting a 25bp hike to 1.25%.
top_catalysts.what_changed: The final pre-decision inflation print is softer than forecast, but the yen is weaker than at the prior Tokyo close and imported-cost pressure remains material.
top_catalysts.why_it_matters: A hike that strengthens the yen without pushing JGB and global long yields sharply higher would confirm that normalization can occur without a new carry shock; hawkish follow-through would challenge the post-Fed relief rally.
top_catalysts.transmission: BOJ rate/guidance → JGB curve and USDJPY → yen-funded leverage → Asian/global duration and high-beta equities.
top_catalysts.confirmation: A BOJ hike accompanied by an orderly stronger yen and contained JGB/global long yields would confirm controlled normalization.
top_catalysts.invalidation: A hawkish path that drives JGB yields and yen funding costs sharply higher, or an unexpected hold that weakens the yen further, would invalidate the controlled-normalization setup.

top_catalysts.event: Oil falls toward $103 Brent even as Saudi pipeline damage expands to three pumping stations, separating tactical logistics relief from structural supply risk
top_catalysts.what_happened: Reuters reported that three pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline were damaged and several sources estimated full repairs could take five to six weeks. Yet Brent fell to about $103.74 in early Asia as partial restoration and Oman loading workarounds reduced immediate scarcity fears.
top_catalysts.what_changed: The damage assessment worsened from two to three pumping stations at the same time that market prices moved lower on expectations for partial capacity recovery.
top_catalysts.why_it_matters: This divergence reveals whether the oil shock is becoming a manageable logistics problem or remains a durable inflation risk that can return once inventories and workaround capacity are tested.
top_catalysts.transmission: Pipeline repair pace / alternative loadings → crude and freight premium → inflation expectations → long yields and central-bank path → risk assets.
top_catalysts.direction: Disinflationary relief with latent geopolitical tail
top_catalysts.confirmation: Verified restoration of material East-West capacity, continued Sohar loadings and Brent holding lower would confirm that logistics are absorbing the outage.
top_catalysts.invalidation: Repair delays, new route attacks or a renewed Brent spike despite partial restoration would show the physical constraint remains dominant.

top_catalysts.event: Post-Fed risk relief broadens as U.S. equities rebound and long yields fall, but Friday quarterly expiry will test whether the move survives event-flow normalization

top_catalysts.event_time_sgt: 2026-09-18 morning after Sep17 U.S. close; Sep18 U.S. session upcoming
top_catalysts.what_happened: The S&P 500 rose 1.14%, Nasdaq 1.69% and Russell 2000 0.55% on Thursday while the U.S. 10-year yield fell to about 4.93%. CME's calendar marks September 18 as the quarterly U.S. equity-index futures expiration date.
top_catalysts.what_changed: The first full post-Fed session reversed much of Wednesday's risk-off move, with technology and small caps participating as both oil and long yields eased.
top_catalysts.why_it_matters: If breadth survives the expiration session and lower yields persist, the Fed hike is being absorbed as a credibility event rather than a funding shock; a reversal would reveal that event and positioning flows exaggerated Thursday's relief.
top_catalysts.transmission: Lower oil/yields + event uncertainty cleared → volatility ↓ / equity breadth ↑ → easier market-based financial conditions; expiry can amplify or distort the signal.
top_catalysts.confirmation: Broad gains beyond mega-cap tech, contained VIX and a 10Y yield staying below the immediate post-Fed area would confirm durable relief.
top_catalysts.invalidation: A sharp expiry-session reversal with volatility and yields rising together would show Thursday's rebound was flow-driven rather than a genuine easing of financial conditions.

geopolitical_risk.label: Geopolitical Risk
geopolitical_risk.change_reason: Partial Saudi restoration expectations are winning in price action despite evidence that physical damage is broader than first assessed.

base_case.label: Base Case
base_case.trigger: BOJ raises the policy rate to 1.25% but signals gradual follow-through; Saudi partial capacity returns and Brent stays near or below the low-$100s.
base_case.expected_market_reaction: Yen firms modestly, JGB yields rise in an orderly way, U.S. long yields remain below the post-Fed peak and global equities keep a constructive but volatile tone.
base_case.what_confirms_it: A controlled yen move, stable cross-market long yields, Brent not reclaiming recent highs and equity breadth holding through the U.S. expiry session.
base_case.what_invalidates_it: A BOJ message implying materially faster tightening or renewed oil-route disruption that pushes long yields and volatility higher together.

bull_case.label: Bull Case
bull_case.trigger: BOJ hikes cautiously, Saudi restoration progresses faster than feared and oil falls below the recent support zone while U.S. long yields continue easing.
bull_case.expected_market_reaction: Global duration rallies, dollar strength fades, small caps and cyclical breadth improve and the equity rally broadens beyond AI leaders.
bull_case.what_confirms_it: Lower oil, lower long yields and broader equity participation persist after the quarterly expiry rather than reversing with flows.
bull_case.what_invalidates_it: Any reacceleration in oil or JGB/U.S. yields that rebuilds the inflation-and-funding feedback loop.

bear_case.label: Bear Case
bear_case.trigger: BOJ delivers a hike with faster-normalization guidance while Saudi repair estimates lengthen or new attacks undermine workaround capacity.
bear_case.expected_market_reaction: Yen funding costs and global long yields rise together, volatility rebounds, high-beta growth and leveraged trades weaken and oil risk premium re-expands.
bear_case.what_confirms_it: A stronger yen accompanied by rising JGB and U.S. yields, higher VIX and weaker equity breadth would confirm a cross-border carry shock.
bear_case.what_invalidates_it: Orderly FX, contained global yields and continued oil declines would break the bear-case transmission chain.

top_catalysts.status: BOJ, oil and post-Fed relief are binding
top_catalysts.summary: BOJ policy, Saudi pipeline restoration and the durability of the U.S. relief rally form today's three highest-conviction cross-asset tests.
paragraphs: The market has moved from anticipating the Fed and BoE to testing whether lower oil and long yields can absorb the final BOJ tightening event without reopening carry stress.

us_macro.title: 美国宏观 / U.S. Macro
us_macro.summary: Weekly claims and regional manufacturing remain firm, while housing construction improves unevenly under near-7% mortgage rates.

central_banks.title: 全球央行 / Central Banks
central_banks.status: Fed/BoE completed; BOJ is today's gate
central_banks.summary: The Fed has restarted hikes, the BoE held hawkishly but softened QT, and the BOJ is the final major decision in the weekly cluster.
paragraphs: BoE's 6-3 hold plus a pause in active gilt sales shows that rate policy and balance-sheet policy can move in different directions. BOJ guidance now determines whether that template extends to Japan or a new carry shock begins.

geopolitics.title: 地缘政治 / Geopolitics
geopolitics.status: Physical damage severe; price premium easing
geopolitics.summary: Saudi pipeline damage is broader than first assessed, but partial restoration and Oman loadings are reducing immediate scarcity.
paragraphs: Three pumping stations are reported damaged and full repairs may take five to six weeks. The falling oil price therefore reflects workaround capacity and expected partial recovery, not a clean resolution of the route risk.

regional_policy.title: 区域政策与中国 / Regional Policy & China
regional_policy.status: Advanced manufacturing and AI self-sufficiency reinforced
regional_policy.summary: China is explicitly prioritizing advanced manufacturing and domestic AI compute capacity, while Japan-US semiconductor investment talks remain active market reporting.
paragraphs: Xi called for a bigger and stronger advanced-manufacturing sector and more controllable supply chains; Huawei says domestic AI-equipment demand exceeds supply and is accelerating its Ascend roadmap. Japan and the U.S. are also reported to be discussing a ¥2–3tn logic-chip factory under the $550bn investment framework.

commodities.summary: Energy is easing while copper and gold show different demand/hedging signals, reducing the one-way commodity-inflation shock.

financing.status: AI financing remains large and rate-sensitive
financing.summary: CoreWeave's $3B convertible and expanded AI-connectivity chip capacity show that the AI buildout is still accelerating despite restrictive policy.
paragraphs: The key distinction is demand versus financing quality: capital remains available, but larger debt and capacity commitments increase sensitivity to long yields, refinancing conditions and eventual cash conversion.

breaking_news.title: Past 24H Major Breaking News
breaking_news.status: BoE/QT shift, Saudi damage update and Japan CPI
breaking_news.summary: The strict past-24-hour window includes the BoE's hawkish hold/QT redesign, a worse Saudi pipeline damage assessment and Japan's final CPI print before the BOJ decision.
paragraphs: These events pull in opposite directions: central-bank language stays restrictive, balance-sheet and energy logistics ease market rates, and Japan's softer core CPI complicates the final expected hike.

market_impact.title: Integrated Market Impact
market_impact.status: Relief rally faces final BOJ/carry test
market_impact.summary: Lower oil, lower long yields and higher equities are now aligned, but the yen and JGB channel can still break that relief pattern.
paragraphs: The cleanest confirmation is cross-asset: if BOJ normalization leaves USDJPY/JGB orderly while Brent and U.S. 10Y stay below recent highs, financial conditions are genuinely easing at the margin. If those variables reverse together, Thursday's rally was tactical.
